<!--
Known issues in v0.2.0-alpha.2, to paste into that release's page on GitHub. This file is not
release notes for a tag: release.yml reads only notes/<tag>.md. Each issue but the last is
fixed in v0.2.0-alpha.3.
-->

### Known issues

- **Sealing a server or nameserver key with a systemd credential makes the service crash-loop.**
  systemd hands the credential over at mode 0440, and alpha.2 refuses any key file that is not
  0600 or 0400. The log says:

  ```
  [keys] unlock: /run/credentials/jig-server.service/jig-server-key is readable by others (mode 440); a credential opens the key, so it must be 0600 or 0400
  ```

  Workaround: seal the keys with a passphrase alone, `deploy/setup-server-key.sh --passphrase-only`
  (and `--nameserver --passphrase-only`), with `JIG_KEY_PASSPHRASE` in the unit's
  `EnvironmentFile=` at mode 0600. That protects the key only as far as the env file is kept
  apart from it. Fixed in alpha.3 (#336).

- **Rotating a server key locks clients out.** After `jig-server keys rotate`, clients refuse the
  server's manifest log and its channels refuse writes. **Do not rotate a server key on
  alpha.2.** If you already have, each client can recover with `jig server forget <server>`,
  which re-pins the server and its log; it also drops that device's other pins for the server.
  Fixed in alpha.3 (#335).

- **Concurrent posts can make a server sign timestamps that run backwards.** Under load on one
  channel, a client may refuse its own server with `chain-clock-backwards`, after which every
  send fails. To recover, run `jig trust evidence list` to see the evidence that was kept; an
  operator can confirm that the two records are the server's own and differ only in clock
  order. Then run `jig trust accept <server>`. Records already signed stay in the chain, so a
  client reading past one for the first time can hit this again, even after the server is
  upgraded.
  Fixed in alpha.3 (#347).

- **A device away for more than about 100 messages on an encrypted channel permanently loses
  the older ones.** The client reads only the newest 100 blocks, and MLS cannot decrypt
  messages that far behind (`cannot decrypt: … Generation is too old to be processed`). There
  is no recovery for messages already skipped on that device. Fixed in alpha.3 (#348): a client
  reads every message it missed, in order.

- **Binaries report the wrong version.** alpha.2 binaries print `0.0.1` for `--version`, and the
  server logs `Starting Jig server v0.0.1`. To identify an alpha.2 or older build, compare its
  file hash with that release's `SHA256SUMS`. Fixed in alpha.3 (#355): from alpha.3 on,
  binaries print the release version, for example `jig 0.2.0-alpha.3`.

- **Legacy peering merges same-named open channels by name.** A post to `#general` on one server
  appears in `#general` on every peered server that has a channel of that name, re-sequenced and
  signed by each receiver. Author signatures still hold, but which server a post was made on is
  lost, and the copies can diverge. It is the pre-contract federation model, in which channels
  are identified by slug alone. Public channels move onto contracts after F2 phase 1, which ends
  it for new posts; #357 tracks posts that have already crossed. Not fixed in alpha.3.
